source.title_on_document: Generative AI and Extended Reality in Collaborative Architectural Design Education: An Exploratory Studio Study

supplement.where: Supplementary Appendices A-C submitted with the article (pp. 18-19); coding framework and coded excerpts on OSF: https://osf.io/dzjc5/overview?view_only=b744989d1db1443fb9b44a9d1cd5efab

paper_design_summary: Twenty-seven sophomore architectural engineering students in seven self-selected teams took part in one undergraduate design studio. Four teams (16 students) were assigned to use GenARch, a pipeline of DALL-E 3 image generation, 2D-to-3D conversion, and multi-user XR review, during Week 3 of a community-gathering-space design task, and three teams (11 students) kept the usual workflow; the paper says the teams were randomly assigned at the team level. A seven-member panel rated the seven recorded team presentations on a 1-5 rubric (including design innovation), and students answered pre/post self-efficacy, collaborative-learning, and teamwork surveys.

studies.label: Studio deployment of GenARch (GenAI + XR) versus usual course workflow

assignment.what_was_assigned: Use of the GenARch GenAI-plus-XR pipeline (with short tutorials) in Week 3 of the course versus the same course workflow without GenARch
assignment.quote: The remaining seven teams were randomly assigned at the team level: four teams (3–4 students each; N = 16) incorporated GenARch into their usual course workflow, while three teams (N = 11) continued the same course workflow
assignment.prereg_locator: No preregistration statement found in the complete 23-page PDF; p. 7, Section 3.5 reports IRB approval only.

arms.name: GenARch
arms.description: Four teams used the GenAI-plus-XR pipeline for ideation and collaborative visualization in Week 3

arms.name: Control
arms.description: Three teams continued the same course workflow without GenARch

participants.exclusions: Two teams declined research participation before randomization because at least one member reported severe motion sickness (p. 6, Section 3.4). The survey-completion-time summaries removed two extreme pre-survey outliers and one extreme post-survey outlier (p. 9, Section 4.1); these are duration-summary exclusions, not stated participant attrition from presentation scoring. Seven team presentations were evaluated (p. 11, Section 4.2). No separate analyzed-person count or post-assignment participant exclusion from presentation scoring is specified. The criterion-specific leave-one-rater-out adjustment concerns raters, not participants (p. 9, Section 3.6).
participants.who: Sophomore architectural engineering students in one undergraduate design studio (35 enrolled in nine self-selected teams; two teams declined because of motion sickness, leaving seven teams and 27 students)
participants.quote: Thirty-five sophomore architectural engineering students were enrolled in the design studio and formed nine self-selected course design teams before study recruitment in September 2025. Two teams declined research participation
participants.locator: p. 6, Section 3.4 Participants; abstract p. 1 (Twenty-seven students formed seven self-selected design teams)

ai_tool.name_model: GenARch pipeline: DALL-E 3 text-to-image; Shap-E, TripoSR, and Tripo3D APIs for 2D-to-3D; Arkio multi-user XR on Meta Quest 3
ai_tool.how_used: Teams prompted by structured web form or speech to generate 2D images and 3D models, then inspected and manipulated selected models together in XR; 15-min tutorial plus 35 min of ideation and asset generation (Class 1), 10-min Arkio tutorial plus 80 min of XR visualization (Class 2)

task.description: Team architectural conceptual design of a community gathering space, with attention to daylight, artificial lighting, and inspiration from nature and everyday experience; outcomes presented as team design presentations
task.duration: Week 3 of the course (GenARch sessions of 35 and 80 minutes); presentations in Class 3 of Week 3

outcomes.name: Panel-rated overall presentation score (mean of five rubric criteria, 1-5)
outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: Seven raters with architectural-engineering backgrounds (two professors and five senior architectural engineering students) evaluated recorded team presentations on a 1-5 rubric. The presentation materials concealed condition, and the paper states that raters could not infer which teams used GenARch (p. 8, Section 3.5 and Table 1). For each criterion, the authors omitted each rater in turn and selected the omission maximizing the increase in Kendall's W; scores were averaged after this adjustment, and condition summaries are medians [IQR] (p. 9, Section 3.6). Overall was calculated as each rater's mean across the five criteria and then summarized within condition after the criterion-specific leave-one-out procedure (p. 12, Figure 4 caption).
outcomes.delay: GenARch ideation and asset generation occurred in Week 3 Class 1, followed by XR visualization and evaluation in Class 2; the recorded design presentations occurred in Class 3 of Week 3 (pp. 7-8, Section 3.5 and Figure 2). This later session evaluates the same course design developed with AI available. An elapsed delay in days is not explicitly reported.

contrasts.reported: Overall presentation score 3.45 [2.89, 3.92] out of 5 for GenARch vs 3.87 [3.63, 3.88] for Control (median [IQR], seven team presentations); GenARch medians lower on all five criteria, between-condition differences not statistically significant. The authors interpret these comparisons descriptively rather than as evidence of a treatment effect.

eligibility.reason: The paper explicitly reports team-level random assignment: four GenARch teams (16 students) and three Control teams (11 students), with 27 participating students overall (p. 6, Section 3.4; abstract p. 1). No separate analyzed-person count is reported, but the entire randomized pool is below 50. Recorded design presentations from seven teams were rated on a rubric including Design Innovation (p. 8, Section 3.5 and Table 1; p. 11, Section 4.2), meeting the output-scoring criterion. The intervention bundles GenAI, XR, and tutorials within the usual course workflow (p. 17, Section 6.5). Two teams declined before randomization because of severe motion sickness; two pre-survey and one post-survey extreme outliers were removed from completion-time summaries (p. 6, Section 3.4; p. 9, Section 4.1). The paper does not specify post-assignment participant exclusions from presentation scoring; criterion-specific rater omissions are scoring adjustments, not participant attrition (p. 9, Section 3.6). Under creativity-codebook.md, Section 3, this randomized experiment with fewer than 50 people belongs in the screening report only, with context_class none.

one_line_finding: In a 27-student studio with seven teams randomly assigned at the team level, GenARch teams had a lower overall panel-rated presentation score than Control (median 3.45 [2.89, 3.92] vs 3.87 [3.63, 3.88] out of 5), and none of the between-condition differences was statistically significant (p. 11, Section 4.2; Fig. 4a, p. 12).
notes: The supporting-materials URL was copied from PDF p. 19; the OSF repository was not accessed. The paper describes a qualitative coding framework and coded interview excerpts and restricts public sharing of additional participant-level data; public availability of quantitative data or code was not verified. Supplementary Appendices A-C are referenced but absent from this PDF and were not read. The four added rubric criteria are coded other because the main PDF names them without the detailed rubric anchors.
